Cautiously hawkish with a more negative growth skew once SLOOS is incorporated. The FOMC raised the target range to 4.75–5%, lifted IOER to 4.9%, and kept QT on track, while noting that recent banking stresses will likely tighten credit. SLOOS evidence reinforces and deepens that outlook: banks report tightening standards on C&I and CRE loans, weaker loan demand across nonfarm nonresidential, construction/land development, and multifamily, and decreased financing needs tied to plant/equipment, M&A, inventories, and accounts receivable; foreign banks also report weaker C&I demand. This broad-based tightening and softer credit demand point to a stronger drag on business investment, hiring, and growth than implied by the statement’s baseline, while supporting disinflation. Standing facilities contain instability but do not offset the restrictive stance. Net tone: more negative than neutral, with an added downside skew to activity relative to the initial read and a disinflationary tilt.
